thread:
ravi: Noticing a pattern: intermittent PCIe rx_errors + nvlink_crc on eu-west edge racks when we co-locate many long-window decoders. Happened twice this week, different tenants. Suspect scheduler packing density + lack of fabric-awareness.

noa: Can you paste the counters? Which hosts?

ravi: Quick snapshot: host-201 rx_errors=97 nvlink_crc=12 dmesg shows repeated nvlink CRC warnings. Host-202 less bad but rising. This correlates with tail token latency spikes for tenants 2100 and 2101.

tess: Sounds like fabric saturation from multi-tenant packing. Current allocator doesn't consider NVLINK/PCIe budget. We should consider a short-term hedge: when nvlink_crc>5 && rx_errors>50, prefer placing new high-concurrency allocs into preemptible lanes or dedicated hot-slices.

infra-bot: Alert: PCI_FABRIC_THRESHOLD host=host-201 rx_errors=97 nvlink_crc=12 severity=high

noa: Immediate mitigation options: 1) soft-quarantine offending tenants (egress throttle + concurrency cap) 2) throttle new allocations that would be packed onto same host 3) scheduler-level quick fix: reduce packing score for hosts with fabric signals. Low-to-high disruption.

ravi: I ran a small experiment: bumped host score penalty for host-201 and queued new allocs to warm pool. Result: no new nvlink warnings for 10m, tail latency stabilized. So scheduler penalty helps. We need a more automated approach.

tess: Proposal: add a fabric-aware heuristic to the scheduler that consumes a new telemetry metric: fabric_health_score. If fabric_health_score<0.7, assign negative affinity and prefer preemptible/dedicated. We can implement as a short-lived feature-flagged change.

noa: Sketch of allocator change (canary): ```bash
# reduce packing on bad hosts
curl -X POST $ALLOC/v1/hosts/host-201/score -d '{"delta":-0.4}'
# route new high-concurrency allocations to preemptible lane
curl -X POST $ALLOC/v1/tenants/2100/actions -d '{"action":"prefer_lane","lane":"preemptible"}'
```
Run on canary zone eu-west-1 first.

infra-bot: Canary job scheduled: fabric-penalty-canary id=canary-827 started by noa at 09:12 UTC

ravi: Canary outcome after 6m: host score penalty reduced new packing, rx_errors stopped climbing, nvlink_crc count plateaued. No user-facing errors observed.

tess: Nice. Follow-ups: - RFC to add fabric_health_score exporter with NVLINK/PCIe signals - allocator change to convert score into placement preference + auto-eviction to preemptible if sustained - add alert runbook mapping suggestions (throttle vs hot-slice vs scheduler-penalty)

noa: Cost tradeoffs: preemptible lanes cheaper but may increase tail latency via eviction. Hot-slice preserves SLOs but costs ~0.6-1.0x extra depending on slice size. We should surface predicted cost in the operator UI when suggesting hot-slice.

ravi: Agreed. I'll file the RFC and include a small dashboard tile: fabric_health_score / recommended_action / estimated_cost_delta. Also add a one-click "apply scheduler-penalty" for oncall.

infra-bot: Action logged: fabric_penalty_canary outcome=success owner=noa ticket=RFC-2026 created

noa: I'll land the canary change behind a feature flag and schedule ramps (zone -> region -> global) once RFC is approved. Runbook note: rollback = remove host score delta and clear tenant lane preference:
```bash
curl -X POST $ALLOC/v1/hosts/host-201/score -d '{"delta":0.4}'
curl -X POST $ALLOC/v1/tenants/2100/actions -d '{"action":"clear_prefer_lane"}'
```

tess: Great. Also add an automated alert augmentation that includes recommended CLI commands so less experienced oncall know the typical steps.

ravi: Thank you. Closing thread after RFC + runbook PRs land.
